author: independent Java technology critics (ten immutable source reports; canonicalized by pep-m-java-methods-evidence-rematerialize)

findings.claim: The static activity awards both mapped objectives without using Temperature.conversions, printing either returned conversion result, or supplying the required explanations.

evidence.section: Understanding Class Members: class variables, class methods, and instance-variable access

findings.recommendation: Bind each class-qualified call result to direct output, require the final print to read Temperature.conversions, and objectively check the explanation/contrast clauses.

findings.claim: The explanation for traditional static main says no object exists when a program starts; the relevant rule is that no particular Main instance is required.

evidence.section: JLS SE 25 §12.1.4 Invoke a main Method
Compact Source Files and Instance Main Methods; delivered in JDK 25

findings.recommendation: Replace the absolute claim with no Main object is required or equivalent, while retaining the accurate Java 25 instance-main boundary.

findings.claim: The practice debugger Step Over ignores enabled breakpoints in called methods and exposes a synthetic second pause on the same caller line, contradicting the documented IntelliJ behavior.

evidence.section: Step Over, Step Into, Step Out, Resume, and nested breakpoints

findings.recommendation: Make one Step Over reach the next executable caller line unless an enabled nested breakpoint intervenes, and remove synthetic post-return pauses.

findings.claim: The writing page marks the required use-void Goal Done without requiring the learner to declare or call any valid void method; valid void work is only optional.

evidence.section: Defining Methods: declarations, parameters, return types, and void

findings.recommendation: Require a bounded valid void declaration and call before marking the objective Done, or narrow the objective to what required work establishes.

findings.claim: The page states the false absolute that every path through a non-void method must reach return; throwing and provably non-completing paths need not return because the body must only not complete normally.
findings.recommendation: Teach that every path able to complete normally must return a compatible value, briefly distinguish abrupt and non-completing paths, and align catalog, recap, metadata, and companion.

findings.claim: The residual feedback says no object exists inside static main, preserving the false absolute even though the corrected core teaching refers to the missing qualifying Main instance.

evidence.section: JLS SE 25 §12.1.4 Invoke a main Method

findings.recommendation: Say no Main object is available for the unqualified score access, then regenerate the deterministic companion.

findings.claim: Method-practice awards testing and refactoring Goals without establishing the claimed behavior: discarded test results and disconnected multiplication, threshold, subtraction, and return witnesses can receive completion.

evidence.section: Defining Methods: declarations, parameters, return types, and void
JLS SE 25 Chapter 15: expressions and integer division

findings.recommendation: Bind each test invocation to its result and prove one connected multiplication → total → strict > 10 decision → branch-only subtraction → returned adjusted value flow, with private regressions.
